limits: Invocation and feed-filter counts are snapshot totals collected before the measured workload, not phase deltas.
Runtime lookup found/missing counts are separate from patch-time target matching.
Patch-time target matching does not establish live endpoint suppression or request counts.
An invocation is not necessarily a blocked event, request or unique advertisement.
This installed extension reports 0.0.5; the snapshot does not validate the audit source baseline or published 0.0.7 bundle.

app_scope_verification.report_scope: Instagram's per-app VPN allowlist, including its mathematically mapped Android SDK sandbox UID.

routing_evidence.source: Saved Android connectivity snapshot before capture stopped

app_scope_verification.mapping_evidence: AOSP Process defines app UIDs starting at 10000 and SDK sandbox UIDs starting at 20000, and maps sandbox to app by subtracting 10000. The observed pair satisfies that mapping. AOSP Vpn.getAppsUids includes corresponding sandbox UIDs automatically in an app VPN allowlist.
app_scope_verification.interpretation: The second routed UID is expected for the allowed application. Its presence is not evidence that an SDK sandbox ran or transmitted traffic.
app_scope_verification.counter_comparison: The separate Android network counters target only the main application UID. The capture allowlist covers that UID and its corresponding SDK sandbox UID and does not distinguish them per packet. Capture and counter windows also have different collection bounds and accounting layers; do not expect equality or add the totals together.
app_scope_verification.privacy: This scope summary includes no raw IP addresses, serials, device identifiers, payloads or credentials.

sources.title: AOSP Process SDK sandbox UID ranges and mapping

whole_capture_summary.capture_continuity: Packet timestamps do not establish capture start/stop or continuous coverage. Zero-count windows and silent tails require independently recorded CaptureService continuity and start/stop evidence.

requested_window.definition: Only packet and byte counts in [start, end) are included. Host mappings are learned across the entire capture.

whole_capture_summary.byte_definition: Declared IP packet length in this capture, including IP and transport headers. Retransmissions remain counted. PCAPdroid VPN mode synthesizes inbound headers and segmentation, so these are not radio/wire bytes or application-upload bytes.
whole_capture_summary.transport_payload_definition: Declared TCP segment or UDP datagram payload bytes, excluding IP and transport headers. Includes encrypted data, handshakes and retransmissions. Does not establish application content or unique uploads. Fragments or incomplete/invalid transport headers are counted as unclassified.
whole_capture_summary.tcp_zero_payload_definition: TCP packets whose declared payload length is zero; their IP-byte total includes only headers. These can include connection control as well as acknowledgments. ACK-only count further requires exactly the ACK flag, with no other TCP flags.
whole_capture_summary.host_definition: Visible ClientHello SNI from TCP TLS or authenticated QUIC v1/v2 Initial. A name does not prove a completed TLS connection, request path, server receipt, or tracking purpose.
whole_capture_summary.direction_definition: Exact source/destination match against the configured local VPN IP addresses. Other packets retain unknown direction.
limitations: Encrypted application contents are not decoded or emitted. QUIC Initial decryption exposes handshake metadata only.
ECH can expose a cover name. No DNS inference, reverse lookup, IP geolocation, TLS key logging, or certificate inspection is used.
TCP and QUIC reassembly is bounded. IP fragments, unknown QUIC versions, encrypted DNS and preexisting handshakes may remain unmapped.
Transport flow counts are distinct endpoint tuples, not proven sessions. Reuse of a tuple can combine connections.
Long opaque labels and local/reverse names are redacted. The raw PCAP may contain private information and stays local.
The API app filter must be independently recorded by the capture operator. This parser cannot prove app attribution from a raw-IP file.

clock_observation.policy: Nominal conversion uses the midpoint of the union of before/after offset uncertainty intervals. Sensitivity uses that entire union, not only the initial reading.
clock_observation.limitation: Actual clock drift between samples is unknown. Overlapping sample intervals do not establish drift. The union covers both measured intervals but cannot exclude an unsampled clock step outside the envelope; no linear interpolation is assumed.

clock.policy: Nominal conversion uses the midpoint of the union of before/after offset uncertainty intervals. Sensitivity uses that entire union, not only the initial reading.
clock.limitation: Actual clock drift between samples is unknown. Overlapping sample intervals do not establish drift. The union covers both measured intervals but cannot exclude an unsampled clock step outside the envelope; no linear interpolation is assumed.

boundary_sensitivity.method: Workload bounds are phase.started_epoch through after-snapshot boundary.started_epoch, excluding after-snapshot collection. Host epochs are shifted into device PCAP time. Fixed clock-shift low/high variants move both bounds together; inner/outer variants bracket independently uncertain boundaries.
boundary_sensitivity.continuity: Empty packet windows do not themselves prove capture continuity. Interpret them with separately recorded CaptureService, app-filter, capture-start and capture-stop evidence.

foreground_interpretation.conclusion: Most received bytes are mapped to cdninstagram.com names. Most sent bytes use UDP. The small TCP header-only share cannot explain most sent bytes. Encrypted QUIC ACK/control frames and application data are not separated, so sent totals do not measure analytics uploads.

background_counter_comparison.interpretation: The capture exceeds the main-UID counters by more than the evaluated clock-boundary sensitivity. Scope includes the mapped SDK sandbox, and VPN capture versus Android physical-network accounting and collection windows differ. These observations do not establish which factor caused the discrepancy or how much each contributed.

limitations: Only the Home-visible, display-on interval is a valid completed background observation. The mixed-screen interval is excluded from this comparison, and aborted intervals have no completed comparison.

Packet silence alone does not prove continued capture. The zero-packet baseline and final 108.7 seconds of background silence require the independent service/start/stop observations. Those observations support the recorded capture interval but are not a continuous service-state trace.
Declared IP bytes include IP/transport headers and retransmissions. VPN mode can synthesize incoming headers/segmentation. They are not physical radio bytes or application-upload bytes.
TCP zero-payload counts include connection control; strict ACK-only counts require only the ACK flag. UDP payload includes encrypted QUIC data and control whose purpose cannot be identified here.

A visible handshake hostname does not prove a completed request, server receipt, content type, or tracking purpose. Names learned across the full capture are assigned by endpoint tuple; tuple reuse can merge connections.
The raw-IP capture lacks per-packet UID attribution. The expected mapped sandbox UID is included by Android VPN routing; its presence does not establish sandbox activity.
Short, sequential phases with capture overhead and different display/app states do not establish a causal battery saving or typical daily behavior.

caveats: Physical charge delta covers the entire phone, including capture software, wireless control and other apps.
Per-app mAh is Android estimated attribution and can be revised or rounded; it is not measured app energy.
VPN history and raw kernel UID counters are reported separately and must not be added to physical-network totals.
BatteryStats network attribution can overlap VPN and underlying traffic; use the primary netstats totals. Modeled app energy may inherit attribution limits.
Background network set, background process state and screen-off time describe different conditions.
UID process-state times are elapsed classification time, not CPU runtime. Background or cached classification does not mean the process performed no work.
Named process CPU overlaps UID CPU; named job runtimes may overlap each other.
UID CPU sums work across cores, so its one-core equivalent can exceed 100%. Wakeup-alarm counters cover the screen-off battery timebase.
A short sequential observation does not establish a causal saving or typical daily battery life.
Fewer than three changes between sampled charge values; gauge granularity and unobserved changes limit interpretation.
No charge-counter step was observed. Zero reported charge change does not mean zero power; the drain rate is unresolved.
Direct per-UID kernel CPU was denied; CPU totals come from synchronized battery accounting.

provenance.method: Review of previously saved snapshots only; no device actions.
input_artifacts: Saved phase metadata and boundary timestamps
Before and after Android diagnostic snapshots
provenance.attribution: Measured app owner-profile UID only; raw UID, account identifiers and PendingIntent handles omitted.
provenance.alarm_time_basis: Device Eastern wall clock converted to UTC and corrected by the midpoint of the measured offset envelope, rounded to whole seconds. About one second clock uncertainty; not trace-synchronized.
provenance.history_limit: Retained AlarmManager and JobScheduler histories are bounded snapshots, not guaranteed complete execution traces.

interpretation_limits: Alarm delivery does not identify its resulting CPU, bytes, power or user-visible purpose.
Non-wakeup RTC heartbeat deliveries must not be described as device wakeups.
Zero screen-off wakeup accounting is uninformative for a screen-on workload.
Registered and ready jobs are distinct from observed job starts.
The stopped baseline was screen off; the accepted app-background phase kept Home awake. Their whole-phone discharge cannot be subtracted to isolate app energy.
The stopped baseline also had an unresolved flat charge counter.
Whole-phone fuel-gauge discharge and Android estimated UID energy are separate quantities.
